# Setup & map

[Course guide](../../docs/course-guide.md) · [Exercise](exercise.md) · [Worked solution](solution.md)

## 00 · Setup & map — 15 min

**Outcome:** Run the offline rehearsal and distinguish a saved agent, a conversation session, and a sandbox.

> The model chooses actions; the runtime executes the loop; tools supply capabilities; the application enforces permissions.

### Teaching beats

- 0–4: show the final brief and the three runtime choices.
- 4–10: install the locked environment, run preflight, and open the fallback.
- 10–15: identify where configuration, state, execution, and permission live.

### Explain and show

- The course uses one paper, one CSV of secondary summaries, shared instructions, and one output schema.
- A saved managed agent stores reusable configuration; a session stores ongoing work; a sandbox is an execution environment. None is an interchangeable ID.
- Managed Agents API, Responses, and Agents SDK are alternatives. Our order is a teaching sequence, not a migration prescription.
- All live paths read OPENAI_MODEL from server configuration, with gpt-6-luna as the course default. Access must be tested for the teaching project.
- The offline runtime is a deterministic teaching simulation. Its successful run is not evidence that a live model works.

### Completed demo

Run from the repository root. Live commands make API requests; choose one prepared runtime rather than running every alternative in class.

```bash
uv sync --extra class --extra app --extra dev
uv run python -m course preflight
uv run python -m course demo --runtime offline --follow-up --output outputs/setup
uv run python -m course replay
```

**Open:** [course/config.py](../../course/config.py) · [course/prompts.py](../../course/prompts.py) · [course/schemas.py](../../course/schemas.py) · [docs/verification.md](../../docs/verification.md)

### Exercise

- Draw four boxes: model, runtime, tool, application. Place choose a function, execute Python, enforce publisher permission, and keep conversation history in the correct boxes.
- Run preflight and the offline demo. Identify a primary-paper citation and explain how a CSV citation differs.
- Name what must be rechecked before moving from offline to each live runtime.

### Expected solution

- The model proposes calls; a runtime coordinates steps; the application tool handler executes Python; application authorization decides whether a requested side effect is permitted. History belongs to the chosen runtime/state strategy.
- paper:N identifies a page from the PDF. record:N identifies an existing secondary CSV summary, not a newly verified paper.
- Check credentials without printing them, model/project access, managed capability access, available budget, and the live verification report. Run preflight --live, then a small runtime smoke test.

**Checkpoint:** Point to the model setting, the tool dispatcher, the brief schema, and the application permission check. Explain why offline success cannot verify API access.

**Fallback:** Use the offline demo and replay. Teach the distinction between deterministic simulation and captured live output explicitly.

**Official references:** [Runtime comparison](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents) · [Agents API concepts](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/overview)
